terms.meaning: From Greek "Oikos" (house) and "Nomos" (management), so literally managing a household.
The ability of goods and services to satisfy wants.
Things in limited supply, so you must pay for them.
Activities people do to earn money and satisfy wants.

items.name: Early Indian economic writing
items.formula: Manusmruti covers farming, tax and revenue.
items.example: Kautilya's Arthashastra, of the Mauryan period, covers finance and administration.

items.name: Father of Economics
items.example: He called economics "the study of Wealth".

items.name: A. C. Pigou on economics
items.formula: Studying it is not only enlightening but also profitable.
items.example: So it helps both knowledge and daily life.

items.name: The problem of choice
items.example: Economics helps you decide what to buy first.

items.name: Questions producers face
items.formula: What to produce, how, for whom and at what price.

items.name: Prices and resources
items.formula: It explains why prices rise and fall, and how to keep them stable.
items.example: It also shows how to use limited land, water and forests with care.

items.name: Production activities
items.formula: Those that make goods and services.
items.example: Farming, fishing, mining, industries and transport.

items.name: Consumption activities
items.formula: Buying and using goods and services to satisfy wants.
items.example: A student buying a pen and writing with it.

items.name: Exchange activities
items.formula: The marketing system that gets goods to consumers.

items.name: Distribution activities
items.formula: Sharing the income from production fairly among the factors of production.
items.example: This includes fixing the price of those factors.

items.name: When an activity becomes economic
items.formula: Doing it for money makes it economic.
items.example: Free tuition isn't; the same tuition for a fee is.

mistakes.text: Economics started as household management, but today it goes far beyond the home.
Kautilya's Arthashastra is about administration and finance, and it was written in the Mauryan period, long before Adam Smith.
Using a pen is consumption, while making pens is production.
